transcript: Okay, so how a heat pump works, start to finish. It takes a liquid that boils at a really low temperature and pushes it through a coil outside, where even cold air is warm enough to boil it into a gas. Then a compressor squeezes that gas, and squeezing it makes it hot, properly hot. That hot gas goes through a second coil indoors, gives its heat up to the water in your radiators, and turns back into a liquid. Then a valve lets the pressure out and it goes back round again. Plain version: it is a fridge running backwards, moving heat from outside to inside instead of the other way.
